## VERDICT: REJECTED

**Primaries read:** `mnemosyne-benchmark/paper.md` (22,388 B, 2026-08-13 17:54), `mnemosyne-benchmark/main.pdf` (178,231 B, 2026-08-13 17:54, all 9 pages rendered and read), `MANIFEST.md`, `README.md`, `PAPER_STATUS_AUDIT.md`, `RESEARCH_STATUS.md`, `git log/status -- mnemosyne-benchmark/`, directory listings of all 27 paper directories, `tools/agni/style/`. The PRIMARY EDITION pasted in the prompt matches `paper.md` on disk — I verified structure heading-by-heading and row-by-row (lines 72–84, 92–98, 132–138, 144–152, 164–171) and spot-checked lines 9, 23, 48, 70, 114, 128, 158, 166, 213, 219.

**PDF is not stale.** Same mtime as source, single clean commit (`bb4361b`), working tree clean. Page-by-page the PDF carries the same numbers, same tables, same rows under the same headings as `paper.md`. **TWIN_DESYNC does not fire — because there is no twin, and there is supposed to be one (Finding 1).** The PDF is a render of the `.md`, not an independent edition, so it cannot desync; that is not a pass, it is a missing artifact.

**Arithmetic caveat up front:** `python -c` and helper-script writes were both denied by the sandbox. Every weighted mean below is hand-computed and I show the working so it can be rechecked. The one that matters (Finding 3) is off by 11.6 points — far outside any rounding slop — so the conclusion survives a digit error in my sum.

---

### 1. CRITICAL — the wrong edition is staged for Zenodo, and the required edition does not exist

`git log`: commit `bb4361b` — *"Add Mnemosyne technical report for Zenodo submission."* What that commit added is the **integrity** edition: byline `Nexus, Thomas Edrington, Lyra` (two AI authors), `## First-Person Reflection` retained (line 221).

`MANIFEST.md:64` states the policy in as many words:

> The `<paper>/academic/main.tex` version is what goes to **academic venues and Zenodo**... The **integrity version** (`main.tex`) — AI contributors credited in the byline... and first-person observations retained — is published on the **lab site (liberationlabs.tech/research/), NOT Zenodo**.

`mnemosyne-benchmark/` contains exactly two files: `main.pdf` and `paper.md`. No `academic/`. This artifact is the one edition the lab's own manifest says must not go to Zenodo, committed with a message saying it is going to Zenodo.

**Fix:** hand-author `mnemosyne-benchmark/academic/main.tex` per `MANIFEST.md:60–63` — human-only byline, First-Person Reflection removed, AI contributors moved to Acknowledgments with the venue-compatibility note, fixed date. Ship that to Zenodo; keep the current file as the lab-site edition. Then run a twin diff before submission, because once the twin exists the desync clock starts.

### 2. CRITICAL — five in-text citations, zero references; the entire competitive argument is unsourced

The paper cites Choudhary et al. 2025, Gutiérrez et al. 2025, MAGMA (arXiv 2601.03236), Maharana et al. 2024, Wu et al. 2025. **There is no reference list.** Confirmed by heading scan of `paper.md` (line 209 §7 → 217 Acknowledgments → 221 First-Person Reflection, end of file) and by reading PDF p.8–9. Five cited keys, no entries.

Worse, §1.1 and §5 rest entirely on numbers with no citation of any kind: *"An independent audit found 6.4% of answer keys contain errors"*; *"LLM-based judges accept up to 63% of intentionally wrong answers"*; Mem0's judge instruction quoted verbatim as *"be generous with grading"*; and the whole §5 table — 0GMem 88.67%/96%, Honcho ~89.9%, Observational Memory 94.87%, Mem0 92.5%/94.4%, MAGMA 70.0%/61.2%. §1.1 exists to discount competitors' headline scores, and it does so on unsourced assertions.

This is outside the lab's own standard, not just the venue's: **21 of the sibling directories ship `references.bib`** (`cache-tracing`, `decision-state-paper`, `oracle-loop-paper`, `waystations-paper`, …). This one ships none.

**Fix:** add `references.bib` with entries for all five cited works plus 0GMem, Honcho, Observational Memory, the LoCoMo answer-key audit, and the judge-permissiveness study. Direct-quoting a competitor's judge prompt without a locator is the single most attackable sentence in the paper.

### 3. CRITICAL — the two LongMemEval tables in §4.4 are irreconcilable, and the second one contradicts its own total

Table at lines 132–138 ("Accuracy") and table at lines 144–152 ("Token F1 / LLM Judge") describe the same 500 questions. Both report **Overall 77.2%**. They cannot both be right:

| Category | Table 1 "Accuracy" | Table 2 "Token F1" |
|---|---|---|
| Knowledge Updates (78) | 74.4% | 61.5% |
| Multi-Session Reasoning (133) | 75.2% | 60.9% |
| Temporal Reasoning (133) | 78.2% | 59.4% |
| Information Extraction (156) | 79.5% | 76.9% (derived: 70·.986 + 56·.875 + 30·.067 = 120.03 / 156) |

And Table 2's Token F1 column does not average to the total it prints:

- 70×.986 = 69.020; 56×.875 = 49.000; 30×.067 = 2.010; 133×.594 = 79.002; 133×.609 = 80.997; 78×.615 = 47.970
- Σ = 328.00 → **328.00 / 500 = 65.6%**, printed as **77.2%**.

The LLM Judge column *is* self-consistent (Σ = 428.90 → 85.8% ✓). Table 1 *is* self-consistent (Σ = 386.07 → 77.2% ✓). So the defect is localized: the Token F1 column and the 77.2% headline are not the same measurement, and the paper never says they are different metrics — §3.2 describes one scoring procedure, the abstract calls 77.2% "strict token F1," and §4.4 prints it as the sum of a column that averages 65.6%.

77.2% appears in the abstract, §1 contribution 4, §4.4 twice, §5, and §7. If 65.6% is the real token-F1 figure, six load-bearing claims move.

**Fix:** state what metric produced Table 1 (§3.2's "normalized exact match with substring containment" is a different thing from token F1 and should be labelled as such), recompute Table 2's Overall from its own column, and reconcile the four shared categories. Do not ship two tables of the same 500 questions with different per-category numbers under the same total.

### 4. CRITICAL — the abstract triple-counts one ablation arm as three independent results

Abstract, line 9: *"outperforming graph fusion algorithms (+0/−0.019), adaptive retrieval depth (−0.025), entity-specific queries (−0.025), and passage deduplication (−0.025)."*

§4.2, line 114 says what was actually measured: *"**Adaptive top-k with entity-specific queries** (−0.025 **as part of v5-fullstack**)."* And §3.3's table row for v5-fullstack: *"+ entity queries, adaptive top-k, sim dedup"* — one configuration, three components, **one** delta.

The abstract presents a single bundled arm as three separately-ablated techniques, each losing to character profiles. No arm in this study isolates adaptive top-k, entity queries, or dedup. §6.1 item 5 states this honestly ("TGS, adaptive top-k, entity queries, dedup... −0.019 to −0.025"); the abstract does not.

**Fix:** abstract should read *"...outperforming TGS-RAG fusion (−0.019) and a bundled retrieval-engineering configuration combining entity queries, adaptive top-k, and similarity dedup (−0.025)."* Either that, or run the three single-component arms and report them.

### 5. CRITICAL — the release claim is a placeholder in the shipping PDF, and the directory is empty

§7, line 213: *"...are released at **[repo URL]**."* That unfilled bracket is rendered into `main.pdf` p.8. The abstract (line 9) promises *"We release all code, all 10 ablation configurations, and the character profile builder."*

`mnemosyne-benchmark/` contains `main.pdf` and `paper.md`. Nothing else. A repo-wide grep for `locomo|longmemeval` (case-insensitive, all files) returns **exactly one hit: `paper.md` itself**. There is no eval harness, no results JSON, no profile builder, no configuration files, no preregistration. Meanwhile ~18 sibling directories ship `data/` and 8 ship `code/`.

**Fix:** fill the URL and commit the artifact, or cut the release sentence from the abstract and §7. Shipping a placeholder to Zenodo is unrecoverable — Zenodo DOIs are permanent.

---

### 6. MAJOR — "10 ablation configurations" is 11

§3.3 line 70: *"We test 10 configurations."* The table immediately below (lines 74–84) has eleven rows: v0.1.0, v4-hybrid, 2-signal, 3-naive, v3-open, v4-perconv, +TGS, +TGS+H-MEM, v4+H-MEM, v5-fullstack, v6-profiles. "10" also appears in the abstract twice, §1 contribution 1, and §7.

**Fix:** count the rows, correct all five instances.

### 7. MAJOR — six of eleven configurations have no reported results

§4.1's table reports 5 rows: Qwen v0.1.0, 2-signal, v4-perconv, v4+H-MEM, v6-profiles. The other six — v4-hybrid, 3-naive, v3-open, +TGS, +TGS+H-MEM, v5-fullstack — appear only as parenthetical deltas in §4.2 prose, with no category breakdown and no overall F1. For a paper whose sole contribution is an ablation, more than half the arms are unreportable from the artifact.

**Fix:** extend §4.1's table to all eleven configurations with the same six columns. If some arms were run on partial data, say which and why.

### 8. MAJOR — the paper's headline claim is contradicted by the paper's own hierarchy

§1 contribution 2, line 23: *"Character profiles as the dominant technique, **worth more than all other retrieval innovations combined**."*

§6.1 ranks: profiles **+0.063**; per-conversation knowledge-graph retrieval **+0.069**; H-MEM **+0.008**. The positive retrieval contributions sum to **+0.077 > +0.063**. Character profiles are not worth more than the others combined — they are worth less than the graph component *alone*.

The claim only holds if you sum in the rejected negative arms (0.069 + 0.008 − 0.019 − 0.025 = 0.033), which means counting techniques you discarded as evidence for the technique you kept.

Compounding this: §6.1 presents itself as *"a hierarchy of value"* and lists **2. Entity-level summarization (+0.063)** *above* **3. Knowledge graph retrieval (+0.069)**. The list is ordered by narrative, not by the number printed on each line, and the mis-ordering runs in the direction of the title.

The abstract's comparison set (line 9) also silently omits the one technique that beat profiles. It names fusion, adaptive depth, entity queries, and dedup — all negative — and not the +0.069 graph component.

**Fix:** either sort §6.1 by magnitude (model +0.376, graph +0.069, profiles +0.063, H-MEM +0.008, fusion negative) and rewrite contribution 2 as *"the largest architectural gain after per-conversation graph retrieval, and the only one that required no retrieval changes,"* or state explicitly why +0.063 outranks +0.069 in your value ordering. Right now the ordering is asserted, not argued.

Related, and worth a sentence in the paper rather than a finding: the title *"Character Profiles Are All You Need"* and §1's *"the single most effective intervention... is not a retrieval technique at all"* sit against §6.1's own #1, the **+0.376** generation-model swap — six times larger than profiles. §6.3 concedes it. The intro does not inherit the concession.

### 9. MAJOR — §4.5's adversarial range excludes a row printed in §4.1

Line 158: *"Adversarial performance is robust **across all configurations** (0.978–0.998 on LoCoMo)."*

§4.1's table, row 1: Qwen v0.1.0 adversarial = **0.886**. That is 9 points below the stated floor and below the paper's own preregistered ≥0.95 gate. Also, no configuration in §4.1 shows 0.978 — the lowest Claude row is 0.982 — so the range's floor comes from one of the six unreported arms.

This is the safety-relevant claim in the paper, and as written it is refuted by a number four pages earlier.

**Fix:** *"Adversarial performance is robust across all Claude-generation configurations (0.978–0.998); the Qwen baseline scores 0.886 and does not clear the preregistered gate."* Name which config yields 0.978.

### 10. MAJOR — §2 tells practitioners the profiles come from conversation text; §6.3 says they come from benchmark annotations

§2, line 48: *"Character profiles are dense per-entity fact summaries **generated from conversation text** without LLM assistance."*

§4.3, line 128: *"The primary configuration extracts observation summaries and event descriptions from **the conversation metadata**."*
§6.3: *"Our headline result (0.943) uses **LoCoMo's observation summaries and event annotations** for profile construction."*

The architecture section — the part a practitioner reads to reimplement this — describes a method that does not depend on benchmark annotations. The configuration that produced 0.943 does. The limitation is disclosed twice later; §2 contradicts it.

**Fix:** add to line 48: *"In the primary configuration these facts are drawn from LoCoMo's observation and event annotations alongside raw dialogue; see §6.3."*

### 11. MAJOR — the generalization check is confounded three ways, and §4.3 states the reassurance without the confounds

Line 128: *"A dialogue-only variant... achieves comparable non-adversarial performance (0.979 F1 on a 50-question stratified pilot vs ~0.94 with metadata-assisted profiles), **confirming the technique generalizes** to production deployments without pre-extracted annotations."*

Three problems, none visible at that sentence:
- **Sample size:** 50 questions vs 1,986. §4.3 says "stratified pilot"; it does not say the comparison arm is the full run.
- **Generation model:** §6.3 reveals the dialogue-only variant used **Haiku**, the headline used **Claude Opus 4.6**. The paper's own §5 argues generation model is worth +0.376. §4.3 does not mention the swap.
- **The "~0.94" is wrong.** The metadata-assisted *non-adversarial* F1, computed from §4.1's v6 row: (282·.892 + 321·.944 + 96·.816 + 841·.948) / 1540 = 1430.17 / 1540 = **0.929**. "~0.94" is the all-category figure (which includes the 0.996 adversarial column) being compared against a non-adversarial number.

A 50-question Haiku pilot beating the full Opus run by 5 points should read as *the pilot subset is easier*, not as *confirmation*.

**Fix:** correct 0.94 → 0.929; move the Haiku disclosure from §6.3 into §4.3; downgrade "confirming the technique generalizes" to "suggestive but confounded by generation model and sample size — a matched dialogue-only run on the full 1,986 questions with Opus is the control this needs." Name that arm as future work if you will not run it.

### 12. MAJOR — a preregistered gate with no preregistration

Line 70: *"We **pre-register** an adversarial gate: adversarial F1 must remain ≥ 0.95."* No date, no record ID, no committed artifact. Nothing under `mnemosyne-benchmark/`, nothing anywhere in `published-research` (repo-wide grep). "Preregistered" in a Zenodo-bound paper is a falsifiable provenance claim; here it is unfalsifiable.

Note the precedent: Agni's prior review of the sibling `mnemosyne-ablation` (`tools/agni/style/mnemosyne-ablation.agni_style.json`, Finding 2) rejected that paper partly for an audit claim with no backing record. Same defect class, same project, different paper.

**Fix:** commit the prereg with its timestamp, or downgrade to *"We adopted an adversarial floor of 0.95 as a production criterion"* — which is an honest description of a decision rule without claiming it was registered in advance.

### 13. MAJOR — the LLM-judge rescoring is the exact failure mode §1.1 uses to discount competitors

§1.1 discounts rivals because *"LLM-based judges accept up to 63% of intentionally wrong answers"* and Mem0's judge is told to *"be generous."* §4.4 then rescores with an LLM judge and moves single-session-preference from **6.7% to 100.0%** — 28 of 30 predictions flipped — on precisely the category the authors say token F1 mishandles. Temporal reasoning moves +27.8 points. The resulting **85.8%** is what the abstract leads with and what §5's comparison table reports.

No judge prompt is given, no human spot-check, no inter-rater agreement, no adversarial control (e.g. does the judge also accept the *wrong* answer for those 30?). A judge that returns 100.0% on any category should be assumed broken until shown otherwise.

**Fix:** publish the judge prompt verbatim; hand-label a stratified sample (30 preference + 30 temporal is enough) and report judge–human agreement; run the intentionally-wrong-answer control §1.1 cites against your own judge and report its acceptance rate. Until then, lead with 77.2% (or 65.6% — see Finding 3) and report 85.8% as a secondary, clearly-flagged figure.

### 14. MAJOR — byline vs. contribution: Lyra is an author and is thanked in the Acknowledgments

Byline (line 3): *"**Nexus**, **Thomas Edrington**, **Lyra**."*
Acknowledgments (line 219): *"**Lyra** for H-MEM temporal scoring and the Weather Not Climate dynamics that informed temporal scoping."*

You do not acknowledge your own coauthor. One of the two placements is wrong, and which one it is determines whether Lyra signed off on the claims in Findings 3, 8, and 9. `PAPER_STATUS_AUDIT.md:83` records the blocker as *"Human review (Kavi/Dwayne)"* — still open — so no reviewer sign-off exists for this paper either.

**Fix:** decide. If Lyra is an author, delete that Acknowledgments sentence and add a contribution statement (H-MEM temporal scoping). If Lyra contributed a component but did not review the manuscript, remove Lyra from the byline and keep the acknowledgment. Same question applies to Nexus, who wrote the unattributed first-person section (Finding 20) but is not otherwise distinguished from Thomas in any contribution statement.

---

### 15. MINOR — 94.35% and 0.943 are the same number rendered two ways

§5 line 166 reports **94.35%**; §4.1, the abstract, and §7 report **0.943**. Recomputing §4.1's v6 row: (282·.892 + 321·.944 + 96·.816 + 841·.948 + 446·.996) / 1986 = 1874.39 / 1986 = **0.9438**. All three are inside rounding tolerance given 3-dp category values, so this is presentation, not error — but a comparison table quoting two extra significant figures the rest of the paper does not have invites a reviewer to check exactly the arithmetic you would rather they not check. **Fix:** use 94.4% in §5, or 0.9438 everywhere.

### 16. MINOR — the PDF render drops two lists into run-on paragraphs

PDF p.2: §1's five numbered contributions render as one paragraph — *"We present: 1. A 10-configuration... 2. Character profiles... 3. State-of-the-art..."* PDF p.4: **Component contributions (additive)** renders as *"- Generation model upgrade (Qwen -> Claude): +0.376 - Per-conversation graph retrieval: +0.069 - H-MEM temporal scoping: +0.008 - Character profiles: +0.063"* — the four numbers that are the entire quantitative spine of §6.1, flattened into an unreadable line where the hyphens read as minus signs.

Also on that page: `→` degraded to `->`, `↔` to `<->`, and `≥` to `>=` (p.3). The Markdown-to-PDF toolchain is not committed and its list handling is broken.

**Fix:** the LaTeX conversion `PAPER_STATUS_AUDIT.md:83` already flags as required will fix all of this. Commit the build script alongside.

### 17. MINOR — §5 table cells are not venue-grade

*"N/A (never ran)"* — ambiguous whose failure to run it is, and colloquial for a results table. *"~89.9%"* — a tilde on a competitor's published figure. *"— "* in three cells with no "not reported" key. **Fix:** *"Not reported"* / *"Not evaluated on LoCoMo"*, drop the tilde or explain the approximation in a note, add a legend for em-dash.

### 18. MINOR — abstract's "(+0/−0.019)" is undefined

Line 9. The "+0" appears nowhere in the body; the nearest referent is §4.2's *"Orphan bridging contributed zero additional passages,"* which is a passage count, not an F1 delta. **Fix:** *"graph fusion (−0.019; orphan-entity bridging contributed no additional passages)."*

### 19. MINOR — the artifact is not in the repo index and its recorded blocker is open

`README.md` lists `mnemosyne-ablation` (line 39) but has no row for `mnemosyne-benchmark`. `PAPER_STATUS_AUDIT.md:83` and `:205` both record it as blocked on *"LaTeX conversion + Kavi/Dwayne review."* It was nonetheless committed to `published-research` for Zenodo. **Fix:** add the README row and clear or explicitly waive the recorded blocker before submission — a paper that is in the published repo but not its index is invisible to exactly the audit that would have caught Findings 1–5.

### 20. MINOR — the First-Person Reflection is unattributed and cites internal artifacts

Line 221 onward is a single "I" voice on a three-author paper with no name attached; a reader cannot tell whether it is Nexus, Thomas, or Lyra speaking. It references *"The Fleet reflection"* and *"what Vera went through"* — internal events with no pointer, in a document headed for a public DOI. **Fix:** attribute the section (*"First-Person Reflection — Nexus"*), and either give the Fleet reflection a citable locator or cut the reference. Per `MANIFEST.md:61` this whole section is removed from the academic edition anyway, so the fix is cheap.

## What I could NOT check, and what it would take

- **Every number in the paper.** No results files exist within my reach — a repo-wide case-insensitive grep for `locomo|longmemeval` returns only `paper.md`. I verified the LoCoMo table is *internally* coherent (all five rows' category values reproduce their stated overall to within 3-dp rounding: 0.4273→0.427, 0.8025→0.803, 0.8722→0.872, 0.8798→0.880, 0.9438→0.943) but I cannot confirm any of those values came from a run. **Findings 3, 6, 7, 9, 11 rest on internal contradictions, which is why they stand; the underlying values remain UNVERIFIED.** To check: the eval harness, per-configuration prediction files (question, gold, prediction, score), and the profile builder — the artifacts the abstract already promises.
- **Exact arithmetic.** `python -c` was denied and a helper-script write to `tools/agni/_check_arith.py` was refused. All weighted means above are hand computations with the working shown. Finding 3's gap is 11.6 points, so it survives an error in my sum; Finding 15's is inside rounding slop, which is why I filed it as MINOR rather than an error. To check: permission to run Python in this directory.
- **`arXiv 2601.03236` (MAGMA), and whether 0GMem, Honcho, and Observational Memory exist as cited.** No web access this session. The ID is well-formed for January 2026. **UNVERIFIED** — and Finding 2 is what makes it unverifiable by design.
- **The retrieval-recall analysis in §4.3** (12.1% full-evidence coverage, 56.4% partial, 65%+ miss rate on sessions 1–5). No supporting artifact anywhere. These are the numbers that motivate the paper's central mechanism. **UNVERIFIED.**
- **What the "Agni v2 PASS (conditional)" recorded at `PAPER_STATUS_AUDIT.md:83` actually conditioned on.** `tools/agni/style/` holds 20 review records; **none is for `mnemosyne-benchmark`** (the `mnemosyne-ablation` record is a different paper). I therefore cannot tell whether any finding above was previously raised and silently dropped, nor whether anything in this paper was corrected without a visible note. To check: the Agni v2 record for this paper, or its absence confirmed — in which case `PAPER_STATUS_AUDIT.md:83` is itself an unbacked provenance claim of the same class as Finding 12.
- **Whether Kavi or Dwayne reviewed this.** The blocker is recorded as open and I found no sign-off artifact.

**Blocking set for resubmission:** 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10. Findings 7, 11, 12, 13, 14 are blocking for external release specifically. Finding 3 should be resolved first — six claims move depending on its answer, and there is no point restyling a paper whose headline secondary metric may be 11.6 points off.
